newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeks to reschedule Paris Club debt.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeks to reschedule Paris Club debt.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim cabinet will seek to reschedule debt payments due to the Paris Club of official creditors this year and may reach a funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) next week, Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said on Wednesday.
Speaking after a meeting between a visiting IMF mission and a financial stabilisation council set up by the interim cabinet to speed up reform, Gavriiski said:
"Tomorrow Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski is going to send a letter to the Paris Club, in which we will ask to reschedule payments which are due this year."
He said that Bulgaria sought to reschedule up to $50 million due from part of the non-rescheduled payments.
Bulgaria has so far paid these amounts regularly, but an economic crisis caused by continuous mishandling of the economy has depleted its reserves.
"Our request to is to roll over these payments for next year. This year every sum of funds is significant for us," said Gavriiski.
Under three agreements rescheduling a $1.2 billion debt owed to the Paris Club by 1995, Bulgaria is due to pay official creditors $126 million this year.
"We would like to start negotiations with the Paris Club for possible rescheduling of the other obligations as well," said Gavriiski.
Bulgaria was likely to reach a preliminary funding agreement with the IMF which will enable the interim cabinet to halt the freefall of the national currency, the lev.
"There are possiblities during the visit of this IMF mission to prepare a programme for the next standby arrangement," said Gavriiski.
"Such a programme can be approved with this government and receive the first tranche of the funding in the term of this caretaker government," he said.
Bulgaria's president appointed the interim cabinet three weeks ago after disbanding parliament and setting early general elections for April 19.
